Hi Sophie — great to meet you yesterday. Quick answers from product/sales perspective: yes, we can support a sponsor-funded credit pool that founders spend as sandbox credits, and we can also issue a one-time conversion voucher that applies to a paid commit (Reserved Capacity) SKU. A couple of practical caveats:

- Conversion voucher is a one-time token that applies to a future purchase and expires 9 months after issuance.
- The conversion path requires a minimum committed value (we typically set a $5k minimum for reserved conversion to ensure predictable capacity).
- We cannot retroactively apply sandbox consumption to a past committed bill — conversion is forward-looking only.

Laura and Ben, looping you in for legal/finance sign-off on the tax wording and the SOW language around "sponsor-funded conversion". Sophie, I flagged the SOW line items that should be edited (section 2.1 and the conversion appendix). If you want, I can produce a short one-paragraph tax note for Ada's team once finance confirms.

Next steps: Laura, can you confirm the tax stance and whether we need Ada's W-9/other tax docs on-file? Ben, would a 9-month voucher expiry with $5k floor work for you from an ops/SLA standpoint?

Thanks —

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Hi all — finance review below. Short answer: we treat sponsor-funded promotional credits as a vendor-funded promo. Tax treatment depends on jurisdiction and how the sponsor structures the grant:

- For US-based corporate sponsors providing promotional credits to founders, we typically classify the credit as a vendor discount. The sponsor provides Redwood with funds or a prepayment; Redwood issues credits to end users. From Redwood's perspective, it's a reduction of revenue recognized (contra-revenue) tied to the sponsoring contract.
- For the receiving founders, whether the grant is taxable depends on local tax law — generally, if the sponsor is providing something of value directly to the founder (and not just paying a vendor), the founder's finance team should treat it as income. Ada should consult their tax counsel for founder-level obligations.

Required operational steps:
1) Ada must sign our Sponsor Addendum (collection of sponsor details + confirmation of funds) and provide a tax intake (W-9 or local equivalent) so our accounting team can correctly route revenue recognition.
2) If Ada wants Redwood to withhold an admin fee (up to 10%), we can implement that: the SOW will show total sponsor commitment, admin fee shown as a separate line, and net credits issued. Admin fee reduces the gross funds and therefore changes revenue recognition amounts.

I'll draft a one-paragraph explainer for Ada to hand to founders and their accountants if that's helpful. Marcus/Ben, I'll put the Sponsor Addendum + the paragraph in the shared Drive.

Thanks —
Laura Bennett
Director, Revenue Operations
